title: Kunti
hook: her sons finally rule, and Kunti walks out of the city toward the forest, with blind Gandhari's hand on her shoulder

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti sent her sons the story of Vidula: better to blaze for a moment than to smolder for a long time. Did one smoldering thing get a first step? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-eight.

A small procession leaves Hastinapura through the gate. In it walks an old blind king, Dhritarashtra, whose sons died in the war. His hand rests on the shoulder of his wife, Gandhari, her eyes bound with cloth. And Gandhari's hand rests on the shoulder of the woman leading them both: Kunti. The Pandavas are on the throne at last. Their mother has everything the war was fought for. And she is walking away from it, into the forest, guiding the parents of the men her sons killed. Her sons run after her. Today: Kunti's last word to them.
screen: `A PROCESSION LEAVES THE CITY.` → `A HAND ON EACH SHOULDER.` → `KUNTI LEADS THEM OUT.`

segments.voice: The scene is in the Mahabharata's Book of the Hermitage. Dhritarashtra has decided to end his days in the forest, and Gandhari goes with him. Kunti's sons assume their mother will stay. She doesn't. Yudhishthira begs her. Bhima puts the hard question into words, here in paraphrase. You roused us to fight. And now that the kingdom is ours, you leave it? Kunti's answer is the center of the scene. I urged you on, she says, so that you wouldn't live on in humiliation, so that Draupadi would not be wronged again, so that the family's name would stand. Not so that I could enjoy a kingdom. I had my time as a queen, with your father. Now I will serve my husband's elder brother and his wife in the forest. Go back. Her answer settles more than one thing. First, it settles a question her sons had. The woman who urged the war wanted none of its prize for herself. Second, look at who she walks with. Gandhari lost her sons in the war Kunti's sons won. And Kunti chooses to be her guide, her hand under Gandhari's. The epic doesn't explain it with a speech. It just shows the two mothers walking together. Third, it's a picture of a life with seasons. There was a time to rule, a time to fight, and now a time to let go, and Kunti seems to know which is which. Tomorrow, the woman with her hand on Kunti's shoulder gets her own days.
screen: `SHE LEAVES THE KINGDOM BEHIND` · `WHY DID YOU ROUSE US, THEN?` · `NOT FOR MY OWN ENJOYMENT` · `TWO MOTHERS WALK TOGETHER`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: the hand on your shoulder. Sit comfortably and let the breath slow. Rest one hand lightly on your own shoulder, or just imagine it there. Let it be the weight of someone you walk alongside: someone you guide, or someone who guides you. Notice whether that person is easy or hard to walk with. Kunti led a woman whose grief her own sons had caused. Just stay with the feeling of the hand for a few breaths. If you pray, you can hold that person in prayer. The bell holds the time.
Kunti. With the kingdom won, she walked into the forest, guiding Gandhari, and told her sons she had urged them on for their honor, not her own enjoyment. Today's word.
Your line: Kunti. Today, offer a hand to someone it's hard to walk beside, the way Kunti led Gandhari out of the city. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: Hindus meet Kunti's departure in fuller retellings of the Mahabharata's later books; the ideal of leaving household life for the forest in old age, vanaprastha, is an old stage of life described in Hindu texts.

original.note: Sanskrit, vanaprastha: the stage of life when one leaves the household for the forest (vana).
